input.rationale: Sharpens the one part of the audit that was still carried as a derivation rather than as an executed observation, and corrects a claim that was looser than the source supports. The parent account says the peers that receive a forwarded compaction recompute the requested bound against their own decided index and, with the same drifted decided index, are read to mirror the leader's loss. Reading the peer-side handler shows the second branch that sentence left implicit: handle_compaction applies the forwarded compaction through the node's own trim or snapshot path and discards the result (mod.rs 217-227, with the comment that errors are ignored because the data will still be kept), while the snapshot path refuses any index above the receiver's own decided index with UndecidedIndex and the trim path refuses any index above its own minimum recorded accepted index. A peer therefore compacts to the leader's index only when its own decided index already covers it - and then builds its own snapshot from its own range, which for the compacting node in the observed receipt was empty - or it quietly keeps its state where it was, which is the opposite of mirroring the loss. The new knowledge entry records both branches with the source that decides them, and the material for the handler is added in the same update; no other record changed, no execution was requested, and the parent account's conditioned sentence remains true as written, now with its other branch named and sourced.

knowledge.statement: A forwarded compaction is applied by each peer independently and its outcome is discarded: SequencePaxos::handle_compaction calls the node's own trim or snapshot path for a Compaction::Trim or Compaction::Snapshot and ignores the returned error, so a peer compacts to the leader's index only when that index is within its own decided index (snapshot) or at or below its own minimum recorded accepted index (trim). A peer whose own decided index lies below a forwarded snapshot index refuses it with UndecidedIndex, the error is discarded and the peer stays exactly as it was; a peer whose decided index covers the index compacts to it and builds its own snapshot from its own storage range, which can be empty when its log holds nothing above its own compacted index.
knowledge.conditions: Leader or follower receiving PaxosMsg::Compaction; the sender is the node that called snapshot or trim with local_only = false, so a cluster-wide compaction reaches every peer but each peer decides for itself. Read from mod.rs 217-227 together with the receiver-side bounds (try_snapshot refuses an index above the receiver's decided index and try_trim refuses an index above its minimum recorded accepted index). No execution sampled a peer receiving a forwarded compaction: every compaction call in this run's receipts used local_only = true or ran on the leader itself, which is why this behaviour is recorded as a source-derived refinement of the parent account's peer-side sentence rather than as an observation.

knowledge.statement: For a candidate that syncs from the greatest promise, the accepted index it ends with is the adopted promise's own accepted count whenever the resume point lies inside that promise's content: sync_idx is the candidate's decided or accepted index, the suffix is the adopted promise's log from there, and the carried StopSign adds the same one index the adopted promise already counted, so the two accounting terms cancel. Whenever the resume point lies beyond that content the suffix is empty and the candidate ends at sync_idx plus the StopSign term. A disagreement between the adopted decided index and the entries held therefore needs some promise reporting a decided index above the adopted promise's content.

knowledge.statement: Trim's bound is the minimum of the leader's recorded accepted indexes and both trim paths respect it: with no explicit index that minimum is used, and an explicit index above it is refused with that same minimum reported. The bound can therefore exceed only the content of replicas whose recorded accepted index has itself drifted; a replica whose report is still truthful keeps the bound at or below its own accepted index, so no in-cluster re-synchronization request can fall below a compacted index that trim produced.

The parent account said peers receiving a forwarded compaction recompute the bound against their own decided index and, with the same drifted decided index, are read to mirror the leader's loss; that sentence is true as conditioned but left the other branch implicit. Reading the peer-side handler shows it: handle_compaction applies the forwarded compaction through the node's own trim or snapshot path and discards the result (mod.rs 217-227, whose comment states that errors are ignored because the data will still be kept), while the snapshot path refuses an index above the receiver's own decided index with UndecidedIndex and the trim path refuses one above its own minimum recorded accepted index. That two-branch behaviour, with the handler material added in the same update and the reason no execution samples it (every compaction in this run was local_only or leader-side), is now recorded as a knowledge entry, so the audit's last derived item is derived explicitly rather than asserted loosely. No other record changed, nothing was executed, and no gaps remain registered: every question in the run carries a current account with its own receipts, controls, counterevidence and limits.
